DISPLACED PERSONS (COMPENSATION AND REHABILITATION) ACT,
1958
ACT XXV111 OF 1958
An Act to provide for the payment
of compensation to certain displaced persons and the rehabilitation of others,
and for matters incidental thereto or connected therewith
[28th March 1958, Gazette,
Extraordinary, 28th March 1938]
The following Act of the National Assembly received the assent of
the President on the 26th March 1958 and was published for general information
in the Gazette.
1. Short title, extent and commencement.-(1) This Act may be called the
Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1938.
(2) It extends to West Pakistan and the Federal Capital.
(3) It shall come into force at once.

2. Definitions.-In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or
context,-
(1) "claim" shall have the meaning assigned to it in the
Registration of Claims (Displaced Persons) Act, 1956, but shall not include a
claim in respect of agricultural land ;
(2) "claimant" means a displaced person whose ;claim
(excluding claim in respect of agricultural land) has been registered under the
aforesaid Act
(3) "displaced person" means any person who, on account
of the setting up of the Dominions of Pakistan and India, or on account of
civil disturbances or the fear of such disturbances in any area now forming
part of or occupied by India, has, on or after the first day of March 1947,
left, or been displaced from, his place of residence in such area and has
subsequently become a citizen of Pakistan, or is residing therein, and includes
any person who, being a resident of any territory outside India, is for that
reason unable to manage, supervise or control any property belonging to him in
India or in any area occupied by India, and also includes the
successors-in-interest of any such person
(4) "house" means evacuee residential premises of any
value in an urban area, or of the value of ten thousand rupees or more in a
rural area, together with the gardens, grounds, garages and outhouses, if any,
attached to or appurtenant to such premises, notwithstanding that any such
garden, ground, garage or outhouse is in the possession of a person other than
the person or persons in possession of such residential premises, but does not
include any residential building situated within the premises of an industrial
concern, or a building or premises declared under paragraph 15 of the First
Schedule, to be a big mansion or hotel;
Provided that where a building not so declared consists of more
than one residential premises, and such premises are in the possession of
several persons, the premises in the possession of any one of such persons
shall be deemed to be a house ;
(3) "local" means a citizen of Pakistan other than a
displaced person ;
(5) "possession", except for the purposes of section 30,
does not include possession obtained on or after the seventeenth day of
February 1958, but includes possession so obtained in pursuance or as a result
of an order passed before that date by the Rehabilitation Commissioner or by
the Custodian;
Provided that a claimant dispossessed of any property on or after
the first day of July 1957, shall be deemed to be in possession thereof.
(7) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under
this Act ;
(8) "prevailing market value" means the amount of the
value of the property as determined by the Settlement Commissioner;
(9) "price determined on evaluation basis" means-
(a) in the case of a house or shop situated within the limits of a
cantonment, an amount equal to twenty-five times the gross annual rent of the
house or shop, as the case may be, prevailing in 1946 ; and
(b) in any other case, an amount equal to forty times such rent ;
(10) "public dues" include-
(a) arrears of rent or any charges due in respect of any evacuee
property allotted to or otherwise occupied by the person concerned, or in
respect of any Government property utilized for rehabilitation purposes and so
allotted or occupied ;
(6) any amount received in lieu of rent of immovable property other

3. Power to acquire evacuee property.' (1) The Central Government may, for any
of the
purposes of this Act, by notification in the Official Gazette,
acquire any evacuee property
within the Federal Capital other than agricultural land.
(2) As and when so required by the Central Government the
Government of West Pakistan shall, for
any of the purposes of this Act, by notification in' the Official Gazette,
acquire such evacuee property, other
than agricultural land situated in the Province (excluding the
Federal Capital), as the Central Government may deem it necessary to
acquire.
(3) On the publication of a notification under subsection (1) or
subsection (2), the right, title and
interest, of any evacuee in the evacuee property specified in the notification,
shall, with effect from the date of
such publication, be extinguished, and the evacuee property shall vest wholly and absolutely in the
Central Government free from all encumbrances.
(4) The Central Government shall prescribe the cases or class of
cases in which, and the
period within which,-
(a) any charge created by a Custodian on any property acquired
under subsection (I) or
subsection (2), or
(b) any decree granted by a Civil Court against such property,
shall be satisfied, and the
manner in which it shall be satisfied.
(5) Notifications under subsection (1) and subsection (2) may be
issued from time to time
and may relate to-
(a) all evacuee property generally ; or
(b) any class of evacuee property ; or
(c) all evacuee property situated in a specified area ; or
(d) any particular evacuee property.

4. Compensation pool.
(1) For the purpose of payment of compensation to claimants in
respect of immovable property other than agricultural land, a compensation pool
consisting of the following shall, subject to the provisions of subsection (2),
be constituted, namely :-
(a) all evacuee property acquired under section 3 ;
(h) sale-proceeds of any immovable evacuee property lying with the
Custodian, compensation paid or payable to the Custodian by the Central or
Provincial Government on the acquisition of any immovable evacuee property under
any law for the time being in force, and consideration money paid or payable on
the confirmation of sale of any immovable evacuee property, ; ,
(c ) public dues of the nature described in sub-clause (d) of
clause.(10) of section 2 and recovered under this Act ;
(d) Government property allotted for rehabilitation purposes and
exchanged with evacuee property with the consent of the Government ; and
(e) arty amount
or property forfeited under section 18.
(2) Immovable evacuee property attached to any charitable,
religious or educational trust, and such other evacuee property as may be
specified in this behalf by the Central Government by notification in the
Official Gazette, shall not form part of the compensation pool constituted
under subsection (1).

5. Rent pool.-(1) For the purpose of payment of compensation to claimants in
respect of unrealized rent of or income from immovable property other than
agricultural land left in India, a rent pool consisting of the following shall,
subject to the provisions of subsection (2), be constituted, namely :-
(a) rents realized from immovable evacuee property other than
agricultural land ;
(b) public dues of the nature described in sub-clauses (a) and (b)
of clause (10) of section 2 and recovered under this Act ;
(c) all profits and income (other than sale-proceeds) received or
derived from any immovable evacuee property other than agricultural land lying
with the Custodian, the Central or Provincial Government or any other authority
;
(d) arrears of rent due in respect of immovable evacuee property
other than agricultural land ; and
(e) such contribution, not exceeding ten crores of rupees, as may
be determined by the Central Government, to be made in such manner as may be
prescribed, from the compensation pool constituted under section 4.
(2) Any taxes on immovable evacuee property payable to the Central
Government or Provincial Government or a local authority shall not form part of
the rent pool constituted under subsection (1),
(3) The rent pool
constituted under subsection (1) shall be utilized in such manner as may be
prescribed :
Provided that a flat rate shall be prescribed for payment of
compensation from the rent pool.

than claimants, a rehabilitation pool consisting of such contribution, not

(2) The rehabilitation pool constituted under subsection (1) shall

9. Appointment of Settlement Commissioners.-(1) The Central Government may appoint
a Settlement Commissioner, and such number of Additional Settlement
Commissioners, Deputy Settlement Commissioners and Assistant Settlement
Commissioners as may be necessary for the performance of duties; and functions
assigned to them by or under this Act and may, by general or special order,
provide for the distribution or allocation of work to be performed by them.
(2) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Settlement
Commissioner shall discharge his functions and perform his duties under the
general superintendence and control of the Central Government.
(3) Subject to the provisions of this Act and to such orders as
may from time to time be made by the Central Government in this behalf,
Additional Settlement Commissioner, Deputy Settlement Commissioner and
Assistant Settlement Commissioner shall perform the duties and discharge the
functions assigned to them by or under this Act under the general
superintendence and control of the Settlement Commissioner.
(4) Pending the appointment of a Settlement Commissioner, the
Central Government may appoint any officer to discharge such functions and
perform such duties of the Settlement Commissioner as may from time to time be
specified by the Central Government.

Determination of the amount of compensation

DISPLACED PERSONS (COMPENSATION AND REHABILITATION) ACT, 1958
DISPLACED
PERSONS (COMPENSATION AND REHABILITATION) ACT, 1958
ACT XXV111 OF 1958
An Act to provide for the payment
of compensation to certain displaced persons and the rehabilitation of others,
and for matters incidental thereto or connected therewith
[28th March 1958, Gazette,
Extraordinary, 28th March 1938]
The following Act of the National Assembly received the assent of
the President on the 26th March 1958 and was published for general information
in the Gazette.
12. Determination of the amount of compensation.-(1) On receipt of an application
under section 11, the authority concerned shall, after making enquiry in the
prescribed manner,-
(a) determine the amount of public dues, if any, of the nature
described in sub-clauses (a) and (b) of clause (10) of section 2 and of the
nature described in the other sub-clauses thereof, recoverable from the
applicant ; and
(b) ascertain the amount of compensation to which the applicant is
entitled, separately under the compensation pool and the rent pool, having due
regard to the prescribed scales of compensation, the nature and value of his
verified claim and other circumstances of the case.
(2) The authority concerned shall then determine the net amount
payable to the applicant from the compensation pool and from the rent pool
after deducting the public dues recoverable from him and such settlement fees
as may be prescribed and shall issue certificates to the applicant to that
effect in the prescribed form;
Provided that all public dues of the nature described in
sub-clauses (a) and (b) of clause (10) of section 2 shall be deducted from the
amount of compensation payable from the rent pool, and those of the nature
described in the other sub-clauses thereof shall be deducted from the amount of
compensation payable under the compensation pool;
Provided further that ..in cases where the amount of public dues
of the nature described in sub-clauses (a) and (b) of clause (10) of section 2
exceeds the amount of the compensation payable from the rent pool, then-
(a) if such public dues are not in excess of the verified claim
under Schedule VI to the Registration of Claims (Displaced Persons) Act, 1956,
they shall be set off against such claim; and
(b) if such dues are in excess of such claim, the amount so in
excess shall be recovered from the compensation payable to the claimant from
the compensation pool.
Explanation.-For the purpose of assessing the amount of the
verified claim under this subsection, the Settlement Commissioner shall take
into account the period up to and including the thirty-first day of December
1957, and, unless the verified claim under Schedule VI to the Registration of
Claims (Displaced Persons) Act, 1956, is in respect of that period, calculate
such amount on the basis of the verified claim.
(3) The amount, if any, deducted under subsection (2) shall be
paid to the persons or authority entitled to receive the same, except the
amount of public dues of the nature described in sub-clauses (a) and (b) of
clause (10) of section 2 which shall be credited to the rent pool, and the
amount of public dues of the nature described in sub-clause (d) thereof which
shall be credited to the compensation pool.

Scale, form and manner of payment of compensation

DISPLACED

ACT XXV111 OF 1958
An Act to provide for the payment

15. Scale, form and manner of payment of compensation.-(1) A claimant, other than a
claimant convicted under section 14 of the Registration of Claims (Displaced
Persons) Act, 1956, shall be entitled to receive payment out of the
compensation and rent pools to the extent of the amounts shown in the
certificates issued to him under subsection (2) of section 12, subject to such
maximum limits, if any, as may be prescribed from time to time.
(2) Subject always to the maximum limits, if any, prescribed under
-subsection (1), a claimant convicted as aforesaid shall be entitled to receive
payment to the extent of seventy-five per cent. of the compensation which would
have been admissible to him had he not been so convicted.
(3) Subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made
thereunder, compensation may be paid ill any one of the following forms or
partly in one and partly in any of the other forms, namely :-
(a) in cash ;
(b) by sale or by any other mode of transfer to the claimant of
any immovable property out of the compensation pool, setting off the purchase
money or the valuation of the property, as the case may be, against the
com6pensation payable to him;
(c) by payment out of the rent pool in accordance with such flat
rate as may be prescribed ;
(d) in such other form as may be prescribed.

16. Payment of interim compensation to certain persons, etc.-(1) Subject to the provisions of
this Act and the rules made thereunder, the Central Government may, by order in
writing, require the Settlement' Commissioner or any other officer specially
empowered by the Central Government in this behalf to prepare, in anticipation
of the settlement of claims, one or more schemes-
(a) for the grant of interim compensation to widows, orphans or
old or infirm persons against verified claims in accordance with the scale laid
down in the Second Schedule ;
(b) for the transfer of immovable property on evaluation basis or
otherwise to claimants, non-claimants or to--als in accordance with the
provisions of the First Schedule ; or
(c) for the making of deferred payments, in accordance with the
provisions of the First Schedule, by persons to whom property is transferred
under this Act.
(2) On receipt of an order under subsection (1), the Settlement
Commissioner or the officer specially empowered in this behalf shall have all
such powers, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, as may be
necessary to enable him to prepare and, with the previous approval in writing
of the Central Government, execute all or any of the schemes prepared under
this section.

17. Payment of compensation in disputed cases.-Where there is any dispute as to
the person or persons who are entitled to compensation under section 15 or
section 16 (including any dispute as to who are the successors in-interest of
any deceased claimant) or as to the apportionment of compensation among persons
entitled thereto, such dispute shall, after necessary enquiry be decided by
such authority as may be prescribed;
Provided that such authority may refer any such dispute for
adjudication to the District Judge within whose local jurisdiction the office
of the authority concerned is situated, and the decision of the District Judge
shall be final.

DISPLACED PERSONS (COMPENSATION AND REHABILITATION) ACT, 1958
DISPLACED
PERSONS (COMPENSATION AND REHABILITATION) ACT, 1958
ACT XXV111 OF 1958
An Act to provide for the payment
of compensation to certain displaced persons and the rehabilitation of others,
and for matters incidental thereto or connected therewith
[28th March 1958, Gazette,
Extraordinary, 28th March 1938]
The following Act of the National Assembly received the assent of

18. Forfeiture, etc.-(1) If at any time any claimant, to whom payment of compensation
has been made in accordance with the provisions of this Act, is convicted under
section 14 of the Registration of Claims (Displaced Persons) Act, 1956, then-
(a) if he was not entitled to any compensation, the entire payment
made to him, and
(b) if he was entitled to a part of such compensation, so much of
it as was not admissible to him plus twenty-five per cent. of such compensation
as would have been admissible had he not been so convicted, shall, upon his
being so convicted, stand forfeited to the Government as if such compensation
had never been paid.
(2) The Central Government or any officer authorised by the
Central Government in this behalf may take or cause to be taken such steps as
are necessary to recover the payment forfeited as aforesaid, and
notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in
force, use or cause to be used such force as may be necessary for the purpose.
(3) For the removal of doubts it is hereby declared that the power
to take steps under this section includes-
(a) in respect of payment made in any form other than cash, the
power to obtain the assistance of the police and the use of the police force ;
and
(b) in respect of cash, the power to recover the amount as arrears
of land revenue.

Settlement Commissioner, a Deputy Settlement Commissioner or an Assistant

powers under this subsection in a case in which an appeal is pending.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, if
the Settlement Commissioner is satisfied that in obtaining an order for payment
of compensation the claimant has used fraudulent means or made false
representation, then, notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the
Settlement Commissioner may, in cases where the whole of such 'order has been
so obtained, reverse the order, and in other cases, modify the order so as to
reduce the compensation to an amount to which the claimant would have been
entitled if he had not used fraudulent means or made false representation.
(3) Any amount paid to a claimant as compensation which he was not
entitled to receive shall be repaid by him, and, if not so repaid, shall be
recoverable from him as arrears of land revenue.
(4) The Settlement Commissioner shall not pass an order under this
section reversing or modifying any . earlier order without giving the person
affected thereby a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
(5) Any person aggrieved by an order made under subsection (2),
may, within thirty days of the date of the order, make an application for the
revision of the order, in such form and manner as may be prescribed, to the
Central Government, and the Central Government may pass such order thereon as
it thinks fit.

Commissioner may, within the prescribed period, either of his own motion or on
an application made to him in that behalf, review and, while so reviewing,
modify, reverse or confirm an order
passed by himself or by any of his predecessors-in-office.
Provided that--
(a) an Additional Settlement Commissioner shall .not review an
order passed by any of his predecessors-in-office without first obtaining the
sanction of the Settlement Commissioner ; and
(b) a Deputy. Settlement Commissioner shall not review an order
whether passed by himself or by any of his predecessors-in-office without first

(2) An order shall not be modified or revered unless reasonable
notice has been given to the parties affected thereby to appear and be heard.

confirming on review a previous order.

officer or authority under this Act or errors arising therein from any
accidental slip or omission may, at any time, be corrected by such officer or
authority.

30. Protection of certain occupants.-(1) Where any local or displaced
person is in possession of any evacuee house or shop which is transferred to
any other person under the provisions of this Act .then, notwithstanding
anything contained in any other law, such person shall, without prejudice to
any other right which he may have in that house or shop, be deemed to be a
tenant of the transferee, on the same terms and conditions as to payment of
rent or otherwise on which he held the house or shop immediately before the
transfer;
Provided that-
(a) it shall be lawful for the transferee to charge a rent on the
basis of the latest assessment of the municipality or local authority, as the
case may be, and
(b) it shall not be lawful for the transferee to eject such
persons from the house or shop for a period of five years from the date of
transfer; notice of which shall be given by the transferee to the tenant within
one month of such transfer by registered post (acknowledgment due).
(2) Where the transferee does not give notice within one month as
required by proviso (b) to subsection (1), the period of five years mentioned .
therein shall count from the date 9f receipt of such notice by the tenant;
(3) Nothing in proviso (b) to subsection (1) shall apply to a
tenant-
(i) who has not, within three months from the date of receipt of a
notice of demand sent to him by the transferee by registered post
(acknowledgment due), paid or tendered the amount of rent or arrears of rent
due for any period after the transfer ; or
(ii) who, after the transfer, has sublet or otherwise parted with
the possession of the house or shop or any part thereof, or has committed acts
which are destructive of or injurious to the property.
(4) On the expiry of the period of five years mentioned in proviso
(h) to subsection (1), or on the contravention of any of the provisions of
subsection (3), whichever is earlier, the relationship of landlord and tenant
between the transferee and the tenant shall be regulated in accordance with the
law for the time being in force relating to such relationship.

Manner of disposal of urban evacuee
property
I---HOUSES
1. A house in the possession of a claimant or a parent,
son, daughter or spouse of the claimant, being a house which such parent, son,
daughter or spouse does not claim under the provisions of this Schedule, and if
there is more than one such house, then, any one of the houses which the
claimant desires to retain, shall be transferred to him at a price determined
on evolution basis.
2. A house in the possession of a local since before the first day
of January 1949, shall be sold to the highest bidder in a restricted public
auction in which non-claimant displaced persons and the local in possession
only shall be allowed to bid;
Provided that if any such local is in possession of more than one
house and has been a successful bidder in the auction of any one of them, he
shall cease to be entitled to bid in the auction of the other house or houses.
3. A house not transferred under paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be
available for transfer to any claimant who applies in that behalf and to whom a
house has not been transferred under paragraph 1, and shall be transferred to
such claimant at a price determined on evaluation basis :
Provided that not more than one house shall be transferred to any
one claimant under this paragraph;
Provided further that if there is more than one applicant for the
transfer of the same house, the transfer shall be effected by drawing lots in
such manner as may be prescribed.
4. Houses not transferred udder paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 shall be
sold to the highest bidder in a restricted public auction in which displaced
persons only shall be allowed to bid.
5. Houses not transferred under paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4 shall be
sold to the highest bidder in an unrestricted public aution.
6. After houses have been transferred under paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4
and 5, those not so transferred shall be disposed of in such manner and subject
to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed.
II.-SHOPS
7. A shop in the possession of a claimant or a parent, son,
daughter or spouse of the claimant, being a shop which such parent, son,
daughter or spouse does not claim under the provisions of this Schedule, and if
there is more than one such shop, then, any one of the shops which the claimant
desires to retain, shall be transferred to him at a price determined on
evaluation basis.
8. A shop in the possession of a local or a non-claimant displaced
person or not retained by a claimant under paragraph 7 shall be sold to the
highest bidder in a restricted public auction in which only displaced persons
and the local in possession shall be allowed to bid;
Provided that if any such local is in possession of more than one
shop and has been a successful bidder in the auction of any one of them, he shall
cease to be entitled to bid in the auction of the other shop or shops.
9. Shops not transferred under paragraphs 7 and 8 shall be sold to
the highest bidder in a restricted public auction in which only displaced
persons shall be allowed to bid.
10. Shops not transferred under paragraphs 7, 8 and 9 shall be
sold to the highest bidder in an unrestricted public auction.
11. After shops have been transferred under paragraphs 7, 8, 9,
and 10, those not so transferred shall be disposed of in such manner and
